title: This Male Fish Merges Into a Female and Her Body Doesn't Fight Back
subject: anglerfish

scenes.text: This male fish fuses into a female for life, and her body doesn't reject him.
Deep-sea anglerfish. Some females are over sixty times longer than the male, and half a million times heavier.
The tiny male bites on. His tissue grows into hers. Then they share one blood supply.
That should be impossible. Our immune system attacks any foreign tissue. That's why transplants fail.
Researchers found many of these males have lost key genes of that immune system, the ones behind tissue rejection.
So he never leaves. He lives off her blood, a permanent part of her.

description:
This male anglerfish fuses into a female for life, and her body doesn't reject him.
In some species the male loses key immune genes, so he can share her blood supply at 300 to 5,000 meters deep.
What's the strangest animal partnership you know?
thumbnail_text: HE FUSES INTO HER. FOR LIFE.
first_comment: There are about 160 known anglerfish species, and not all of them fuse. Would you want an immune system like this?
